names.kimball_house_1801_prairie: 1801 Prairie Avenue — W. W. Kimball's Chateauesque house in Bedford stone, built at the massing J. W. Taylor's c. 1895 photograph shows

source.citation: Harold Allen for HABS, 'View: exterior - from NW, north (18th St.) and west (Prairie Ave.) elevations', W. W. Kimball House, 1801 South Prairie Avenue, Chicago, June 1965. HABS IL-1077 photograph 2 of 3 (call number HABS ILL,16-CHIG,75--2). Library of Congress.
what_it_does_not_supply: the 1904 state of anything altered between 1904 and 1965 (the window air-conditioners are 1960s; the fence and the street furniture are not read)
the rear (east) wall or the court side: the camera cannot see them
what_it_supplies: the east range's north face whole, from the gabled section to the north-east turret: its wall height, its slate roof and its stone wall dormers, its door and its openings, through the solved camera
a second camera on the 18th Street flank and the front's north end, to check the Taylor print's readings
